readerTitle: The Dutch nurses who fired their managers' stopwatch
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Buurtzorg, 네덜란드 방문 간호) + 실제 연구 (자기결정이론, 대학 모금 콜센터 연구) + 가상 적용 (대기업 내 팀, 회계·자문 회사)
insight: 사람을 움직이는 힘은 보상만이 아니라 스스로 정할 여지, 실력이 늘고 있다는 느낌, 일이 누구에게 도움이 되는지 보이는 것에서 나온다. 이 세 가지는 일의 설계로 만든다.
misconception: 의욕이 떨어진 팀은 돈이나 보너스, 더 촘촘한 관리로 살린다. 자율을 주면 통제를 잃는다.

sources.text: Buurtzorg Nederland, company materials on self-managing nursing teams (founded 2006 by Jos de Blok)
Deci, E. L., & Ryan, R. M. (2000). The 'what' and 'why' of goal pursuits: Human needs and the self-determination of behavior. Psychological Inquiry.
Grant, A. M., et al. (2007). Impact and the art of motivation maintenance. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes.
Pink, D. H. (2009). Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us. (자율·숙련·목적이라는 표현을 대중화한 책)

factChecks.note: Buurtzorg 설립 연도(2006), 설립자 Jos de Blok이 간호사 출신이라는 점, 팀당 최대 약 12명 구성은 Buurtzorg 공식 자료로 다시 확인하세요. 간호사 수는 자료마다 다르므로 카드에는 "thousands of nurses"로만 적었습니다.
설립 전 네덜란드 방문 간호가 작업 단위·시간 기준으로 쪼개져 있었다는 설명은 널리 인용되는 내용이지만 표현을 일반적으로 유지했습니다. 구체적 분 단위 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다.
코치(coach)가 여러 팀을 지원하고 관리자는 두지 않는다는 구조, 작은 본사 조직은 공식 자료로 확인하세요. 본사 인원 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다.
Grant 등(2007) 모금 콜센터 연구: 장학금 수혜 학생과 짧게 만난 모금원들이 이후 통화 시간과 모금액이 늘었다는 결과. 구체적 증가율은 카드에 쓰지 않았습니다. 원문으로 연구 설계를 확인하세요.
자기결정이론의 세 욕구는 원래 autonomy, competence, relatedness입니다. 이 레슨의 '자율·숙련·목적'은 Pink(2009)의 대중화된 표현이며, 카드 5에 두 틀의 관계를 밝혔습니다.

cards.title: The Dutch nurses who fired their managers' stopwatch
body: In much of Dutch home care in the early 2000s, a nurse's day was split into timed tasks: a bandage here, an injection there, then on to the next address.
One nurse, Jos de Blok, thought the clock was the problem. In 2006 he started a company with no managers at all. It is called Buurtzorg, Dutch for *neighborhood care*.

image.label: A nurse on a bicycle leaving a stopwatch behind
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 네덜란드 주택가 골목을 자전거로 달리는 간호사, 뒤쪽 길바닥에 커다란 스톱워치가 놓여 있음. 따뜻한 오후 빛. 실제 회사 로고나 유니폼 표시는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your best people keep leaving.
body: You run a 10-person home-care team inside a large care provider. Visits are planned by head office and timed in minutes. Nurses say they feel like a production line. Two quit last month.
You can make one big change this quarter. Which one?

options.text: A bonus for nurses who finish the most visits on time
options.feedback: It rewards the exact thing nurses dislike: racing the clock. You may get faster visits and even less reason to stay.

options.text: A pay raise to match the best-paying rival
options.feedback: If pay is below market, fixing it removes a real reason to leave. But it doesn't change the work that's driving people out.

options.text: Let the team plan its own patients and schedules, within budget
options.feedback: You give up some central control. In return, nurses get to use their judgment, which is what they say is missing.

cards.title: Small teams, whole patients, no boss.
body: Buurtzorg was built around teams of up to about 12 nurses. Each team serves one neighborhood and runs itself. Nurses decide who visits which patient, plan their own schedules, hire new colleagues and solve problems together.
Instead of handing out tasks, a nurse looks after the whole person, including family and neighbors who can help. The goal is to make the patient able to manage without them.
The company grew to thousands of nurses across the Netherlands and became a widely studied model.

cards.title: Autonomy, mastery and purpose
body: Beyond fair pay, three things keep people engaged in their work.
**Autonomy:** some say in how the work gets done. **Mastery:** the feeling of getting better at something that matters. **Purpose:** seeing who the work helps and why.
The old timed-task system squeezed out all three. Buurtzorg's design put them back in, without a single extra euro of bonus.

image.label: Three overlapping circles: autonomy, mastery, purpose
image.brief: 깔끔한 인포그래픽. 겹치는 원 세 개에 "Autonomy", "Mastery", "Purpose" 라벨. 각 원 안에 작은 아이콘(방향을 고르는 손, 올라가는 계단, 사람을 향한 하트). 가운데 겹치는 부분에 "Engaged work".

cards.title: Decades of research point the same way.
body: Psychologists Edward Deci and Richard Ryan spent decades testing what they call self-determination theory. People do their best work when they feel in control, feel capable and feel connected to others. Writer Daniel Pink later popularized the shorter label *autonomy, mastery and purpose*.

Purpose can be surprisingly concrete. In one study by Adam Grant and colleagues, university fundraising callers briefly met a student whose scholarship their calls had funded. In the weeks after, they spent more time on the phone and raised more money.

cards.title: You don't need to remove managers.
body: Buurtzorg is an extreme version. Most businesses can add the three in smaller doses.

A warehouse team can choose how to lay out its own pick zones. A bakery can let a junior baker own one product and improve it. A sales team can hear directly from a customer the product helped. Each move hands over a decision, builds a skill or makes the impact visible.
cards.softwareNote: For engineering teams, this often means giving a team a problem to solve rather than a list of features to build, time to improve their tools, and regular contact with the users who rely on their work.

cards.title: Freedom without support is just neglect.
body: Autonomy works when people have the skills, the information and a clear goal. Buurtzorg teams are small, share one clear aim and get help from coaches and simple shared tools. Take those away and "self-managing" can become confusion.
These three also don't replace fair pay. If people feel underpaid, talk of purpose can sound like an excuse. Fix the basics first, then design the work.
cards.callout: Hand over decisions in steps, as skill and trust grow.

cards.title: Now it's an accounting firm.
body: You run a 25-person firm that does bookkeeping and tax work for small businesses. Junior accountants spend all day on reconciliations a partner then reviews. They rarely speak to clients. Engagement scores are falling.
What's the best first move?

options.text: Give each junior one client to own end to end, with weekly partner check-ins
options.feedback: They get a real decision, a skill to build and a client they can see helping. The check-ins keep quality safe while they learn.

options.text: Add monthly team dinners and a spot bonus for error-free work
options.feedback: Nice gestures that may lift mood for a while. The work itself stays the same, so the effect tends to fade.

options.text: Let juniors pick any clients they want and drop partner reviews
options.feedback: Lots of autonomy, but without the skills or a safety net. Errors on tax work can hurt clients and the firm.

cards.title: Design the work, not just the reward.
body: People stay engaged when they can decide something, get better at something and see who it helps. All three come from how you shape the job.
**Try it today:** pick one role on your team. Write down one decision you could hand over, one skill they could build and one way they could see their impact.
